title: Perturb a fixed point.
prompt: Run x[n+1] = a x[n] with x₀ = 0.01 for a = 0.5, then change a and run again. Compare contraction with amplification.
hint: Try a = 2 on the second run. The fixed point 0 remains fixed in both models.

conclusions.text: A fixed point being unchanged guarantees that nearby states move toward it.
Nearby behavior depends on the multiplier; being a fixed point alone is not enough.
Any nonzero perturbation changes the mathematical rule.

feedback.pass: A fixed point and its neighborhood answer different questions. The finite plots motivate, but do not replace, an all-time stability argument.
feedback.fail: Both rules fix zero. Compare what happens to the nearby state rather than to zero itself.
